claims.text: The funding opportunity is for UK universities to establish a Leverhulme Research Centre.
The centre should conduct outstanding original research aiming for a step-change in scholarship.

Up to £10 million is available for up to 10 years.
Eligible institutions are universities in the UK registered by the Office for Students and holding their own research degree awarding powers.
A Leverhulme Research Centre can be based at a single university or a collaboration between multiple institutions.
Each UK university can submit one application as a principal applicant but can be a partner in multiple proposals.
The participation of international institutions is encouraged but not required.
The Trust encourages higher-risk, fundamental, curiosity-driven, and multi-disciplinary research.
The choice of research topic is open, but medical and clinical research are ineligible.
The chosen topic should be large-scale enough to support an ambitious research agenda for up to ten years.
Leverhulme Research Centres should not duplicate existing activity at a comparable scale.

Institutions hosting a centre must provide office and workspace and other university support.
The Trust does not fund on a full economic costing basis.
Increases in costs over the lifetime of the centre must be managed within the awarded funding.
The Trust will not award follow-on funding; persistence beyond the original award is at the initiative of the grant holder or institution.
Prospective applicants should follow their university's internal selection process first.

The chosen applicant will be given access to the Grants Management System to begin their outline application.
Invitations for full-stage applications are expected in September.
The deadline for full-stage applications is at the end of the year (of 2027).
Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant based in a UK university who will act as Director.
Applications are considered via a two-stage process: an outline bid and a detailed proposal.
The outline bid includes a short form and a five-page description of the centre's structure and research activity.
The description should include the research area, key research questions, and how the centre will contribute.
The description should detail the centre's structure, including single or multi-site, institutions involved, and key staff.
The description should justify the choice of principal applicant and senior staff.
The description should indicate how resources might be used over the centre's duration.
Shortlisted outline bids will be invited to submit a detailed proposal and a statement of support from the institution.
Shortlisted full applications will lead to an interview.
Final decisions are anticipated to be made by the Trust Board.
The Trust is unable to provide feedback on applications.
